cards.html: This skill covers the problem that push notifications solve and the mental model behind them. If you only remember this skill, you should still not misuse FCM.

You ship a small app with your own login and your own FastAPI backend. One feature needs to tell a user something now: a friend nudged you, a long job finished, a model drifted. The phone is in a pocket and the app is closed.

First attempt: the app polls GET /api/nudges every few minutes. It works, but Android will not run a background job more often than about every 15 minutes, so "now" means "within a quarter of an hour".

cards.s: Why polling and sockets fall short
cards.html:
ApproachWhat goes wrong
Poll on a timerAndroid limits background work to roughly every 15 minutes, and each poll wastes battery when there is nothing new
Keep your own socket open from a background serviceThe OS, or the phone maker's battery saver, kills it, and every app doing this drains the battery
Ask the user to open the appDefeats the point of a nudge

Phones solved this by running one shared, OS-managed connection to a push gateway, and letting every app ride it. On Android, Google's gateway is Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM). It is one product inside Firebase, Google's bundle of app-backend services.

 Your server (FastAPI)            Google                  Phone
 ────────────────────     ────────────────────     ───────────────────
 "user bob → token T9"──► FCM gateway          ──► Play Services (one shared
  POST messages:send       (stores it, retries)      always-on connection)
                                                          │
                                                          ▼
                                                    your app wakes for a few seconds
                                                    → shows a notification / rings

cards.s: What FCM does and does not do
cards.html:
• It transports a small message from your server to one app install.
  • It does not know your users, store your data, or guarantee delivery. Design as if a message can arrive late, or not at all.
  • Think of it as a mailbox service with a courier you do not control.

quiz.q: Why can a closed app get a push within seconds, while its own polling job cannot?
o: The phone keeps one shared OS-level connection that every app rides
FCM keeps your app running in the background
quiz.why: Your app is woken by the OS when a message arrives.

o: Transports a small message from your server to one app install
Stores your users and their data
quiz.why: It is a pipe, not a database or a login.

quiz.q: Push notifications are guaranteed to be delivered.
quiz.why: Myth. Delivery is best-effort, so keep the truth in your own backend.

quiz.q: Why is polling every few minutes a poor fit on Android?
o: Background work is limited to roughly every 15 minutes
quiz.why: So 'now' becomes 'within a quarter of an hour'.
